doc: Keepsakes journal (SPEC.md §7.11, docs/lore/SLICE.md §7, docs/lore/LOWE.md §7, docs/lore/KETTLE.md §7, docs/lore/TARNHALL.md §7, docs/lore/THORNWOLD.md §7). A thread starts when its first step's flag is set; the journal shows every step whose flag is set, in step order. Lines are verbatim from SLICE.md, LOWE.md, KETTLE.md, TARNHALL.md and THORNWOLD.md.

steps.line: Ingra is a sack of rye short and blames a dog.
The rye was in the byre, under the dog. It had been his bed.
Ingra said he was a good dog.
Ingra is counting bowls.
Brede lost a cork float off the herring net.
The float was in the ice, where the tide stopped.
Brede says the wrong knot on the back makes it lucky.
Brede is mending the net himself.
Hesk dropped his good tongs in the bog, raking for iron.
The tongs were frozen into the bog, jaws down.
Hesk said they were never that good, and took them.
Hesk says the wind has come right.
Aud ties heather on Orm's mound every evening, the last one on the road.
Orm's cord was in the first barrow on the road.
Aud says Orm tied his knots too tight to read.
Aud has moved her heather to the first mound. She says it was always there.
Ivo is harnessing the dogs and says he is not going anywhere.
Ivo says he can hear the ice through his feet.
The supper was still on the hook. The ladle was frozen standing up in it.
Ivo says the line holds either way round.
The mitten was in the ice where the hole had been, palm up.
Ivo put the mitten on. Both of his are his own now.
Halla keeps her cargo on a knot-cord and says every knot on it is hers.
Halla's cord was tied to the mooring post. There was a knot at the end in another hand.
Halla read the last knot and called Sten over, and then told him to stay where he was.
Halla has put Sten by the fire in the end house.
Lusse is on the ninth verse of the goat song and wants the chorus from everyone.
Lusse had the chorus out of you. She said it was nearly right.
The guest-tally was on the inside of the door-post. The last knots were one knot, tied over and over.
Lusse counted the tally twice and got two numbers, and started the goat song again from the first verse.
Ottar has his boots on to row home before dark. He has had them on since noon.
Ottar's stick was leaning inside the barred door, where he left it so as not to forget it.
Ottar says the other stick is his wife's, and that she is at home.
Ottar took his stick back and sat down again for the end of the song.
Somebody opened the doors, and Ottar went and stood in them.
Linnet and Eyvind cannot agree where the gate goes. Neither of them wants to.
The birch ring was in the ash at the eastmost clamp. Linnet took it off to work.
At the grave was a knotted cord. Nobody here could read it.
Lusse read Linnet's cord. It is an Outsong, tied by the one it was for.
Old Calder makes the flock forty-four. Sigga makes it forty-three.
A pair of boots stood by the sheiling door, toes to the wall. The door was on the latch.
The fold-tally was by his hand at the cairn. Forty-three notches, and one cut small.
Calder says the boots are his. He says he has his on.
Four knucklebones were in the turf by the small grave on the cliff. The set has five.
There was a knucklebone in the middle of the drove-road, on the side going east.
Wren has a set like it. One of hers has a bite in it. She says she did it.
The coal is still alight.
The flowers went down the water. Wren watched them out of sight.
